title: Data2Story per-asset media provenance manifest (S2 canonical block)
_doc: ONE shared shape for every sourced media asset's provenance, so the Scout, the Designer, and the fetch scripts (fetch_stock.py / fetch_openverse.py / fetch_images.py / fetch_music.py) all speak it. This is the 'S2 canonical media manifest block'. It is the same object `validate.py`'s media check and the Designer's `data-sct`/`data-des` registration rule are written against — keep them in lock-step. The gold World Cup blog's assets/cinematic_imagery_manifest.json is the real-world reference instance (it carries two extra cinematographer fields — `category`, `suggested_beat`, `orientation` — that are allowed but not required here). A side-loaded manifest is only a scratchpad: an asset is not 'registered' until it is also a keyed item in scout.json (sct_*) / designer.json (des_*) carrying this same license+identity. The license gate is the allowlist: re-host an asset only when license.spdx is on scout/references/license_allowlist.json AND license.permits_republication is true; identity.verified must be true for any specific real subject.

id.description: Stable provenance id, prefixed by the registering role: sct_* (Scout) or des_* (Designer). This MUST match the key under which the asset is registered as an item in scout.json / designer.json — the side manifest and the role JSON share the id.

file.description: Local path to the downloaded asset, relative to PROJECT_DIR (e.g. 'assets/bg_stadium_floodlit.jpg'). For an embed (player carries its own license) this block does not apply — use scout.json's embed_url instead; the validate.py license gate skips embeds.

source_url.description: The human-facing landing/page URL the asset came from (e.g. the Unsplash/Pexels photo page, the Commons File: page). NOT the raw CDN/binary URL — this is the click-through provenance link a reader can open to confirm the source.

site.description: Short human-readable provider name, used in attribution + provenance UI.

spdx.description: License identifier. For re-hosting it MUST be on scout/references/license_allowlist.json `allow` (CC0-1.0, CC-BY-*, CC-BY-SA-*, PD/PDM-1.0/Public Domain, or the stock licenses Unsplash-License / Pexels-License / Pixabay-License). NC/ND and 'All Rights Reserved' are rejected by the gate.

permits_republication.description: True ONLY for assets you may legally re-host (license on the allowlist). validate.py hard-fails any re-hosted asset whose permits_republication is not true. Copyrighted tracks/clips -> use an embed instead, never this block.

requires_attribution.description: True when the license requires crediting the author (all CC-BY / CC-BY-SA). False for CC0/PD and for the stock licenses (Unsplash/Pexels/Pixabay) where attribution is appreciated but not required. Either way, populate attribution_text.

attribution_text.description: Non-empty, footer-ready credit string: photographer/author + source + license, e.g. 'Photo: Jane Doe / Unsplash (Unsplash License - free commercial use, no attribution required)' or 'Photo: A. Author / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)'. Must be non-empty even when requires_attribution is false (courtesy credit + provenance). The Designer's registration rule rejects an empty attribution_text.

method.description: How the asset's subject was proven, by the cheapest sufficient method (see scout/references/media_verification.json). 'oembed' for embeds, 'trusted_source' for a Wikidata-QID/Commons page naming the subject, 'vlm_view' for opening the image with the Read tool and confirming it depicts the subject (and is a real photo, not an AI render of a real thing).

verified.description: True only when one identity method passed. validate.py HARD-REJECTS any asset depicting a specific real person/place/object whose identity.verified is not true. For generic/ambient imagery (no specific real subject) it may be true with subject describing the generic scene.

subject.description: The real-world subject this depicts, or a one-line description of the generic/ambient scene (e.g. 'Levi's Stadium at night' or 'a football resting on pitch grass; generic, no players'). For stock photos, note whether the scene is illustrative/generic vs a verified specific venue, and end with whether it is a real photograph (not AI).
